title: Progressive Jog and Movement Series
objective: Develop a progressive warm-up that prepares players for progressive whole-body movement while increasing physical and football intensity without creating unnecessary fatigue.
groundSize: 15 metres by 15 metres | Length: 15 metres | Width: 15 metres
time: Minimum: 6 minutes | Recommended: 8 minutes | Maximum: 10 minutes
coachingDifficulty: 1 – Simple organisation with minimal observation or intervention
setup:
• Mark two 20-metre lanes with movement changes at 5-metre markers.
• Organise players so repetitions are continuous and queues remain short.
• Provide a clear walking recovery or run-off route away from active players.
• Demonstrate the first repetition at low intensity before players begin.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Begin with one coach-led walkthrough so every player understands the route, movement or football action.
2. Jog the first lane at 40 per cent while completing arm swings and ankle rolls.
3. Return using side shuffles and controlled backpedal sections.
4. Repeat with skips, high-knee runs and low lateral steps.
5. Complete two progressive run-throughs at approximately 60 and 75 per cent.
6. Rotate starting positions or roles after each repetition or short work period so every player experiences the full activity.
7. Increase intensity only after the group demonstrates control, spacing and correct technique.
8. Finish with one or two repetitions that match the next training or match demand, then move directly to the next activity.
coachingPoints: Raise intensity in clear stages rather than beginning at training speed.
Keep the head, trunk and hips balanced during every direction change.
Use short preparation steps before turning, stopping or accelerating.
Maintain relaxed arm action and efficient foot placement.
Keep all groups moving so players do not cool down in queues.
Coach the specific focus of progressive whole-body movement rather than adding unrelated exercises.
Modify range and speed for players returning from injury or managing restricted movement.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players become progressively warmer without visible fatigue.
Whether posture and balance remain stable as speed rises.
Whether movement quality improves across rounds.
Whether queues or collisions interrupt continuous movement.
Whether any player needs a modified range, speed or direction.

commonErrors.correction: Set explicit intensity targets for each round and require a controlled first pass.

commonErrors.error: Players use long steps before changing direction.
commonErrors.correction: Widen the preparation zone and coach several short control steps.

commonErrors.error: Groups wait too long between repetitions.
commonErrors.correction: Add a second lane or reduce the number of players in each line.

commonErrors.error: The activity becomes a generic run rather than the named movement focus.
commonErrors.correction: Restate the purpose of progressive whole-body movement and remove unrelated actions.

progressions: Increase the final movement speed without reaching maximal effort.
Add a late visual direction cue.
Carry or receive a football during the final phase.
Link two movement patterns in one repetition.
regressions: Reduce travel distance and movement speed.
Use walking versions for returning players.

Players remain balanced through direction changes.
Movement is continuous with little standing time.
The group finishes warm and ready rather than fatigued.
